issue.title: TUI Beads pane refresh is O(epics x issues) and forced every 10 s: 2.8 s per tick today, ~48 s at 4x the store
issue.description:
`load_beads_snapshot` groups phases under epics with a nested scan: for every epic it re-scans all issues (`for epic in project_epics: sorted(issue for issue in issues if PHASE and parent_id == epic.id)`), which is O(epics x issues). `BeadsPane.on_refresh` then calls `self._request_load(force=True)`, bypassing the existing store mtime key, so the full load (list + ready + blocked = three full event-store replays, plus the grouping) re-runs on every 10 s auto-refresh while the pane is visible.

Reproduce: open the Artifacts -> Beads pane on the sase project (7,034 beads, 949 epics) and time one refresh, or run a replica of beads_data.py:141-154 over the store's issues. Measured (research cld, verified by the lead): load_project_beads 2.24 s + grouping loop 0.56 s = ~2.8 s per refresh at 1x; at 2x the grouping alone is 3.41 s, at 4x 37.9 s (refresh ~48 s, longer than the 10 s interval, holding the GIL).

Fix: group phases by parent_id in one dict pass (O(n)); drop force=True from on_refresh so the store mtime key decides whether to reload. Optionally derive ready/blocked from a single store snapshot instead of three replays (ready/blocked semantics are core logic, so that part goes through sase_core).

task_type_fields.impact: Every visible Beads pane tick costs ~2.8 s of replay and GIL-held grouping today and grows quadratically (8.2 s at 2x, ~48 s at 4x the current 7,034 beads), stalling the ACE UI.

issue.creation_reason: Found while measuring bead-store scaling: the Beads pane refresh grows quadratically with the store and ignores its own change key, so it will outrun its refresh interval as beads accumulate.

payload.description: Same class of O(corpus) ACE refresh work that the typing-lag epic fixed elsewhere; the Beads pane was not in its scope
